coverage: All eighteen scenes: full named cast, contextual disguises and mistaken identities, separate family references, staff, reported people, songs and classical/biblical allusions.

entities.name: Viola
entities.body: The play’s main character, Sebastian’s twin sister, shipwrecked on the coast of Illyria.

snapshots.body: The main character, Sebastian’s twin sister, serving Orsino under the name Cesario.
The main character, Sebastian’s twin sister and Orsino’s intended bride; Cesario is her assumed name.

entities.name: Sebastian
entities.body: Viola’s twin brother.

snapshots.body: Viola’s twin brother and Olivia’s husband.

entities.name: Orsino
entities.body: The Duke of Illyria, who is courting Olivia.

snapshots.body: The Duke of Illyria, now intending to marry Viola.

entities.name: Olivia
entities.body: The wealthy countess whom Orsino is courting, and Sir Toby’s niece.

snapshots.body: The wealthy countess, Sir Toby’s niece and Sebastian’s wife.

entities.name: Sir Toby Belch
entities.body: Olivia’s uncle, a resident in her household and Sir Andrew’s drinking companion.

snapshots.body: Olivia’s uncle, now married to Maria.

entities.name: Sir Andrew Aguecheek
entities.body: Sir Toby’s companion, the knight seeking Olivia’s hand.

entities.name: Maria
entities.body: Olivia’s waiting-woman, who keeps watch over the household’s unruly guests.

snapshots.body: Olivia’s waiting-woman and Sir Toby’s wife.

entities.name: Malvolio
entities.body: Olivia’s steward, responsible for managing her household.

entities.name: Feste
entities.body: Olivia’s jester, labeled Clown in the dialogue.

snapshots.body: Olivia’s jester, also appearing under the clerical name Sir Topas.

entities.name: Antonio
entities.body: The sea captain who helps Sebastian.

entities.name: Valentine
entities.body: Orsino’s attendant, sent to Olivia on his behalf.

entities.name: Curio
entities.body: One of Orsino’s attendants.

entities.name: Fabian
entities.body: A member of Olivia’s household and Sir Toby’s companion.

entities.name: Viola’s captain
entities.body: The captain who helps Viola after the shipwreck.

entities.name: The Priest
entities.body: The clergyman Olivia brings to solemnize her vows.

entities.name: The first officer
entities.body: One of the Illyrian officers who arrest Antonio.

entities.name: The second officer
entities.body: The other officer taking Antonio into custody.

entities.name: Olivia’s servant
entities.body: The attendant announcing Orsino’s messenger at Olivia’s house.

entities.name: Olivia’s handmaid
entities.body: The unnamed attendant who gives Olivia’s reply to Valentine.

entities.name: The shipwrecked sailors
entities.body: The sailors with Viola and the captain on the coast.

entities.name: The musicians
entities.body: The musicians attending Orsino’s household.

entities.name: Sebastian of Messaline
entities.body: The father of the twins Viola and Sebastian.

entities.name: Olivia’s father
entities.body: The deceased count, father of Olivia and her brother.

entities.name: Olivia’s brother
entities.body: The brother whose death Olivia is mourning.

entities.name: Titus
entities.body: Orsino’s nephew, mentioned in the account of the naval fighting.

entities.name: Dick the surgeon
entities.body: The surgeon Sir Toby asks for after being injured.

entities.name: Mistress Mall
entities.body: The woman whose curtained portrait Sir Toby uses as a comparison.

entities.name: Quinapalus
entities.body: The invented authority Feste cites in his joke about wisdom and folly.

entities.name: Pigrogromitus
entities.body: The invented figure in Feste’s nonsense, recalled by Sir Andrew.

entities.name: The Vapians
entities.body: The imaginary people in Feste’s nonsense about crossing the equinoctial.

entities.name: The Myrmidons
entities.body: Achilles’s warriors in Greek legend, incongruously invoked by Feste.

entities.name: Peg-a-Ramsey
entities.body: The figure in a popular song whose name Toby applies to Malvolio.

entities.name: The man in Babylon
entities.body: The man mentioned in Sir Toby’s song fragment.

entities.name: The lady of the Strachy
entities.body: The woman whose marriage to a servant Malvolio cites as a precedent.

entities.name: The wardrobe servant
entities.body: The man said to have married the lady of the Strachy.

entities.name: Sowter
entities.body: A stock hound-name used in Fabian’s metaphor about Malvolio following a scent.

entities.name: The Sophy
entities.body: The Persian ruler referred to by his title in the characters’ comparisons and boasts.

entities.name: Capilet
entities.body: Sir Andrew’s gray horse.

entities.name: The hermit of Prague
entities.body: The supposed hermit in Feste’s invented anecdote.

entities.name: King Gorboduc
entities.body: The legendary British king named in Feste’s anecdote.

entities.name: Gorboduc’s niece
entities.body: The supposed niece addressed by the hermit in Feste’s anecdote.

entities.name: Robin
entities.body: The man addressed in Feste’s song.

entities.name: The Egyptian thief
entities.body: Thyamis, the bandit in Heliodorus’s romance, invoked in Orsino’s comparison about jealousy.

entities.name: The Brownists
entities.body: The religious separatists invoked in Sir Andrew’s comparison.

entities.name: Pythagoras
entities.body: The Greek philosopher associated here with the migration of souls between living creatures.

entities.name: Arion
entities.body: The legendary musician rescued at sea by a dolphin.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The goddess invoked in Orsino’s description of Cesario’s appearance.

entities.name: Mercury
entities.body: The Roman messenger god, invoked by Feste.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: Jupiter, the king of the Roman gods.

entities.name: Penthesilea
entities.body: The Amazon queen whose name Sir Toby uses to address Maria.

entities.name: Lucrece
entities.body: The Roman Lucretia, associated with chastity and invoked through Olivia’s seal.

entities.name: Pandarus
entities.body: The go-between in the story of Troilus and Cressida.

entities.name: Cressida
entities.body: Troilus’s beloved, invoked in Feste’s joke about begging.

entities.name: Troilus
entities.body: The Trojan lover of Cressida.

entities.name: Vulcan
entities.body: The Roman smith-god, used as a comparison for a smoke-blackened face.

entities.name: Eve
entities.body: The first woman in the biblical creation story.

entities.name: Saint Anne
entities.body: The saint traditionally identified as the Virgin Mary’s mother.

entities.name: Jezebel
entities.body: The biblical queen whose name Sir Andrew uses as an insult.

entities.name: Noah
entities.body: The biblical survivor of the Flood.

entities.name: Legion
entities.body: The collective demonic name in the Gospel story of possession.

entities.name: Satan
entities.body: The devil, invoked in the characters’ jokes and accusations.

entities.name: Beelzebub
entities.body: The demonic figure Feste invokes, named here as Belzebub.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The deity invoked in the characters’ prayers and exclamations.

entities.name: The Vice
entities.body: The comic tempter of older morality plays, evoked in Feste’s song.

entities.name: The Egyptians
entities.body: The people evoked in Feste’s reference to the biblical plague of darkness.
